children: has told the Guyana government it needs more offshore gas than expected to maximize oil output, potentially leaving less for liquefied natural gas production and exports, Reuters reported Tuesday.

Guyanese officials are now considering whether to downsize a planned LNG project or skip exports altogether and use the gas for domestic power and petrochemical facilities only, according to the report.

However, the consortium has forecast it will need ~2 Bcf/day of gas for reinjection into oilfields ​so it can meet crude output targets at its projects, which would constrain supplies for any gas export projects, the report said.
Instead of the 6M metric tons/year of capacity initially planned, the project reportedly may now have to start with as much as 3M tons/year and expand later.
Separately, Guyana is poised to surpass 1M bbl/day in crude oil exports for the first time this December, when the country starts shipping its Uaru grade crude, Bloomberg reported.
Uaru exports reportedly are scheduled at 4M barrels in December, which would boost Guyana’s total monthly shipments to 33M barrels, equivalent to 1.06M bbl/day.
The first cargo of Uaru, produced by the Errea Wittu floating production vessel, is due to load on December 11-12, the report said.
